standard.title: Create and edit experimental literary texts
standard.description: create and edit literary texts, that may be a hybrid, that experiment with text structures, language features and literary devices for purposes and audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students create and edit literary texts experimenting with language features and literary devices (AC9E7LE07). They have not yet created hybrid texts that experiment specifically with text structures, or focused editing on structural integration of experiments.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and edit literary texts, including hybrids, that experiment with text structures, language features and literary devices for purposes and audiences.

nodes.label: Experimenting with text structures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create a literary text that makes a deliberate structural experiment and can explain what the experiment is intended to achieve.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a short literary text that makes one deliberate structural experiment (e.g. non-linear timeline, subverted genre opening, hybrid form) and explain the purpose of the choice.
nodes.typical_width: Create and draft a literary text that experiments with at least one text structure element and one language feature or device, explaining how the choices serve purpose and audience.
wider: Create a text that adapts an existing short story, poem, play or speech into a different form (e.g. print to short film, poem to spoken word piece), examining what is preserved and what must change
Experiment with prequel or sequel writing as a form of textual intervention — examining how the original text constrains and enables the new one

response_modes.reason: Creative experimentation requires a repertoire of structural options to choose from. Students who have only experienced linear prose structures will default to them. Building familiarity with a range of structural possibilities — non-linear, hybrid, genre-subversive — enables genuine experimentation.

success_criteria: Student makes at least one identifiable structural experiment in the text
Student can articulate what effect the structural experiment is intended to create
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have only experienced linear prose structures default to them — without a repertoire of structural options, 'experimentation' at N1 is impossible, and N2 editing for structural coherence has nothing to edit.

nodes.label: Editing for structural and device coherence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit a literary text to ensure that structural experiments, language features and devices work together coherently, including checking that repetition and detail are purposeful.
nodes.minimum_width: Edit a draft literary text to address at least one coherence issue — checking that detail or repetition is purposeful, that paragraphs are linked, and that run-on sentences are controlled.
nodes.typical_width: Edit a literary text by checking for run-on sentences, ensuring detail and repetition are used for effect, ensuring paragraphs are linked in ways that develop the narrative, and ensuring that structural and device experiments serve rather than undermine the text.
wider: Engage in peer editing with attention to whether another writer's experiments are achieving their stated purpose — developing evaluative criteria for creative editing
Edit across multiple drafts and reflect on what each round of editing reveals about the gap between intention and effect

response_modes.reason: Editing is a precision skill — students can understand the principles but need practice under compositional conditions. Editing for structural and device coherence (not just error correction) requires fluency with both the craft and the revision process.

Effective editing requires students to coordinate attention to grammar, structure, devices and audience simultaneously — holding the text's purpose in mind while attending to local decisions. This is the most demanding compositional capability of the descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The interplay between creative intention and editorial execution is genuinely rich for Y9. Advancing students can develop sophisticated revision practices — not just fixing errors, but refining and sharpening experiments — which is one of the most transferable writing capabilities the curriculum can build.
success_criteria: Student's edited text shows evidence of deliberate revision decisions (not just surface error correction)
Student can identify at least one editing decision that improved the text's coherence or the effectiveness of an experiment
